selectedVariantName: Core Minimal Installer + Optional Addon Packages (NSIS)
decisionReasoning: Core Minimal Installer (NSIS) reduces initial download size by 58% (from 380 MB to 160 MB) while preserving full offline capability.
Heavy optional dependencies (Docling extraction engine ~350 MB) are decoupled into downloadable or demand-loaded addon packages.
Per-user non-admin installation is fully supported, bypassing UAC restrictions on locked enterprise workstations.
All automated lifecycle transitions (clean install, in-place upgrade, component repair, uninstallation) passed 100% verification.
User database and document embeddings in AppData/DATA_FOLDER are preserved across upgrades and uninstalls.
System WebView2 Evergreen runtime detection is integrated with silent bootstrapper fallback.

advantages: 58% reduction in initial installer download size (from 380 MB down to 160 MB).
Decouples heavy optional dependencies (~350 MB Docling extraction engine) into separate addon packages.
Supports per-user installation without requiring Windows Administrator (UAC) privileges.
100% offline installation capable without network dependencies.
Preserves user databases and application data in AppData/DATA_FOLDER during upgrades and uninstalls.
disadvantages: Users requiring document extraction must download or install the Docling addon package separately.
Requires clear UI indication when an optional addon feature is not yet present.
tradeOffAnalysis.mitigation: The application runtime detects missing optional addons (e.g. Docling) and gracefully falls back to lightweight standard text extractors while displaying a one-click addon installation prompt.
